newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 29.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 29.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australis' plan for a merger with Foxtel is expected to head for another court battle, with Optus Vision, the other player in the industry, denouncing the merger. Optus is expected to start legal proceedings later this week. In other news, Moody's said it had put Australis' ratings on review with an uncertain direction and Standard & Poors said it had put its ratings on creditwatch positive.

The U.S. Justice Department may challenge News Corp's plans to acquire Heritage Media Corp. in a $1.35 billion stock-and-debt transaction, the two companies said on Monday. The department's antitrust field office in San Francisco has recommended that the department challenge the deal, the companies said in a joint press release.
Australian paging group Matrix Telecommunications Ltd said late on Monday it would raise A$48.6 million through a one-for-two renounceable right issue at A$0.80 a share.

The Western Australian state government said on Monday it would defer the introduction of a planned gold royalty. Premier Richard Court said the royalty would now be phased in from July 1, 1998, at a rate of 1.25 percent, representing a nine month delay from the original implementation date. Also the gold price rose about US$3 an ounce overnight.
Computershare Ltd said on Tuesday it has bought Ernst & Young Registry Services Pty Ltd and KPMG Registrars Pty Ltd for A$39.75 million from their parent accounting firms.

Fijian-based gold miner Emperor Mines Ltd said on Monday that its 1996/97 (June-July) net profit slumped to A$1.07 million from A$9.53 million a year ago. The company said its unaudited fourth quarter net profit of A$1.17 million after abnormal items included a A$9.44 million profit from hedging.
